J3/J8 servo headers: pin1 GND, pin2 servo power Net-(D2-K), pin3 signal. J3 pin3 net with R3.1 and R13.2. J8 pin3 net with R4.1, R13.1, R14.2. R13 between J3 and J8 signal. R14 between /TTL and J8 signal. Wait spec: R13, R14 when shorted bridge J3-pin3 and J8-pin3 together and onto MAX3485 TTL bus. Netlist: R13 connects J3 pin3 to J8 pin3. R14 connects /TTL to J8 pin3. So if both shorted, J3 and J8 tied to TTL. Correct. But note R14 only connects TTL to J8, and R13 connects J8 to J3. If only R14 shorted, J8 to TTL, J3 not. But spec says both. Fine.

PWM path: R3 from /PWM1 to J3 pin3. R4 from /PWM2 to J8 pin3. /PWM1 net has R9.1 R10.1 R3.2. R9 connects /PWM1 to /PWM1_C1 (J1/J2 pin19). R10 connects /PWM1 to /PWM1_C2 (pin21). /PWM2 net has R11.1 R12.1 R4.2. R11 to /PWM2_C1 (pin20), R12 to /PWM2_C2 (pin22). Spec says R9-R12 select which bus pin (pin 19/21 for ch1, pin20/22 for ch2) supplies PWM1/PWM2. Note schematic annotation: "Short R10, R10 for Core2 and CoreS3 / Short R9, R11 for others" (typo R10,R10 likely R10,R12? Let's parse). Spec table: R9–R12 0Ω jumpers select which M5Stack bus pin (pin 19/21 for ch.1, pin 20/22 for ch.2) supplies PWM1/PWM2 — schematic note: "Short R10, R10 for Core2 and CoreS3 / Short R9, R11 for others" (i.e., GPIO-to-bus-pin mapping differs by M5Stack core variant). Hmm netlist has R9 pin19, R10 pin21 for PWM1; R11 pin20, R12 pin22 for PWM2. The note says Short R10, R10 for Core2/CoreS3? likely typo should R10,R12? For others R9,R11. That matches: Core2/CoreS3 use pin21 for PWM1 and pin22 for PWM2? Others use pin19 and pin20. Netlist supports. No anomaly.

Serial: U1 MAX3485. Pins:
1 RO -> /RXD2 (J1/J2 pin16). Correct receiver output to M5 RX.
2 ~RE and 3 DE tied to Net-(Q2-C) with R7 to GND. Q2 collector. Q2 emitter +3V3, base via R2 to /TXD2, R1 from +3V3 to /TXD2. Need analyze auto direction. Q2 PNP: emitter +3V3, base driven by TXD2 through R2, with R1 pull-up to +3V3. When TXD2 idle high (3.3V), base emitter ~0, Q2 off, collector pulled low by R7 20k -> DE/RE low (receiver enabled, driver disabled). When TXD2 low, base pulled low via R2, Q2 turns on, collector high -> DE high, RE high (driver enabled, receiver disabled). This is standard. R1 10k pull-up to +3V3, R2 5.1k. Fine.

U1 pin4 DI -> /TXD2. Correct.
U1 pin5 GND.
U1 pin6 A -> /TTL net with R6 to +3V3 (2k) and R14 to J8 signal. U1 pin7 B -> Net-(U1-B) with R8 to +3V3 (2.2k) and R15 to GND (2.2k). Wait RS-485 A/B bias: A pulled up, B pulled down. Here A pulled up via R6 2k to +3V3. B pulled up via R8 2.2k to +3V3 and down via R15 2.2k to GND. That gives B midpoint 1.65V, A 3.3V? Actually A pulled up to 3.3, B divider to 1.65. Differential A-B ~1.65V. But standard fail-safe bias: A pulled up, B pulled down. Here B has both pull-up and pull-down, so B at mid, A high. That still gives A>B. But why R8 to +3V3? Spec says R6, R7, R8, R15 bias/pull network on A/B and DE/RE. It lists R6 2k, R7 20k, R8 2.2k, R15 2.2k. It doesn't specify exact connections. Could be intended? Let's think. In many MAX3485 auto-direction circuits, A/B lines have fail-safe bias: A pulled up to VCC, B pulled down to GND. R6 2k from A to +3V3, R15 2.2k from B to GND. What is R8? Maybe R8 from B to +3V3? That would be odd. Or R8 from A to B? Let's inspect netlist: R8 pin1 +3V3, pin2 Net-(U1-B). R15 pin1 Net-(U1-B), pin2 GND. So B has 2.2k pull-up and 2.2k pull-down. A has 2k pull-up only. This creates A=3.3, B=1.65, differential 1.65. It also loads B with 1.1k to 1.65V. Is that a design error? Maybe intended to provide bias? Standard RS-485 termination/bias: A pull-up, B pull-down. Having B pull-up too reduces differential but still okay. But could be a mistake: R8 should be from A to B? Or from B to GND? Wait spec says R6, R7, R8, R15 are bias/pull network on MAX3485 A/B differential lines and DE/RE enable line. It doesn't give exact. The netlist has R8 from +3V3 to B. That is a pull-up on B, which is opposite of fail-safe. But with R15 pull-down, B is mid. Is this an anomaly? Need determine if it would make board behave differently. It might still work but reduced noise margin. However spec says "bias/pull network" not exact. Could be deliberate? Let's not jump.

Also note U1 pin6 A is connected to /TTL, which goes to R14 to J8 signal. U1 pin7 B is not connected to servo bus? Wait RS-485 half-duplex uses A and B differential pair. But serial servos (RS304MD, SCS0009) are half-duplex TTL serial, not RS-485 differential? The spec says "shared half-duplex TTL serial bus, driven through a MAX3485 RS-485/RS-422 transceiver". Hmm MAX3485 is RS-485 differential, not TTL. But maybe they use only A line as single-wire TTL? Let's examine. U1 A pin6 goes to /TTL, which through R14 to J8 signal. U1 B pin7 has bias network but not connected to servo bus. So they use only A output/input as single-ended? That is unusual. MAX3485 driver outputs differential A/B; receiver inputs differential A/B. If B is biased to mid and not connected to bus, A is driven relative to B? The servo bus is single wire TTL, referenced to GND. Using only A and leaving B at mid may not work as TTL. But spec explicitly says MAX3485 converts UART to shared single-wire TTL serial servo bus. Maybe they use A as single-ended? Let's think: MAX3485 A/B are differential; if B is tied to a bias voltage (1.65V) and A swings 0-3.3, receiver sees differential. But the servo bus is single wire, so servo signal is A? The servo expects TTL 0-5V? MAX3485 output A is differential with B; if B is not connected to servo, the A voltage relative to GND may not be full 0-5? Actually driver drives A and B complementary. If B is loaded with bias network but not connected to servo, A will still swing. But the servo's signal input is single-ended relative to GND, so it sees A. Could work if A swings 0-3.3. But MAX3485 is 3.3V, so TTL 3.3. Serial servos may accept 3.3? Maybe.

Wait spec says "shared half-duplex TTL serial bus, driven through a MAX3485 RS-485/RS-422 transceiver". That is odd but maybe they use MAX3485 as a line driver for single-wire? Let's inspect netlist: U1 pin6 A -> /TTL -> R14 -> J8 pin3. U1 pin7 B -> only bias. So yes only A used. Is that intended? The spec says "the two servo signal pins are bridged into one shared half-duplex TTL serial bus, driven through a MAX3485 RS-485/RS-422 transceiver". It doesn't explicitly say both A and B connect to bus. But a MAX3485 transceiver's A/B are differential; using only A is not standard. However maybe the original design does this? Need see if anomaly is something else.

Let's inspect all components for wrong values/types. C1-C4 100u, C5 0.1u. D1 SS54, D2 PMEG3030EP. Q1 IRLML6402 P-MOS. Q2 BC857 PNP. R1 10k, R2 5.1k, R3/R4 1k, R5 47k, R6 2k, R7 20k, R8 2.2k, R9-R14 0, R15 2.2k. All match spec.

Potential issue: Q1 battery switch. Netlist: J5 pin1 -> Q1 source pin2 and R5 pin2. Q1 drain pin3 -> /BAT. Q1 gate pin1 -> R5 pin1 and SW1 pin2. SW1 pin3 -> GND. SW1 pin1 unconnected. R5 between gate and source (J5 pin1). So when SW1 open, gate pulled to source via R5 -> Vgs=0, P-MOS off. When SW1 closed (pin2 to pin3 GND), gate pulled to GND through switch, but R5 also between gate and source. Source is battery voltage. Gate low -> Vgs negative -> on. Correct. But note SW1 pin1 unconnected. SPDT switch: pin2 common, pin3 one throw to GND, pin1 other throw unconnected. So switch either connects gate to GND (on) or leaves gate floating? Wait when switch in other position, pin2 connects to pin1 (unconnected), so gate is only pulled to source via R5, off. Correct. Optional switch. Fine.

Potential issue: J5 battery connector pin2 GND, pin1 to Q1 source. Correct.

Potential issue: D1 orientation. Netlist: D1 pin1 K on +5V, pin2 A on J7.1. So external 5V at J7 anode, cathode +5V. Correct. D2: pin2 A on +5V, pin1 K on servo rail. Correct.

Potential issue: C3 pin1 on Net-(D2-K), pin2 GND. C1 pin1 GND, pin2 Net-(D2-K). C2 pin1 GND, pin2 Net-(D2-K). C4 pin1 GND, pin2 Net-(D2-K). All okay (unpolarized).

Potential issue: J6 PortB: pin1 GND, pin2 +5V, pin3 /PORTB1, pin4 /PORTB2. Spec says J6 GND, +5V, two GPIOs. Correct.

Potential issue: J7 external 5V: pin1 to D1 anode, pin2 GND. Correct.

Potential issue: R13/R14 serial jumpers. Netlist: R13 between J3 pin3 and J8 pin3. R14 between /TTL and J8 pin3. If both populated, J3 and J8 tied to /TTL. But note R14 connects /TTL to J8 pin3, and R13 connects J8 pin3 to J3 pin3. So yes. However if serial mode, R3/R4 (1k series from PWM nets) are still connected to J3/J8 pin3. If R9-R12 are populated for PWM, then PWM nets are connected to bus, potentially loading. But assembly mode likely leaves R9-R12 open in serial mode? Spec says mutually exclusive: PWM mode populate R3/R4 and appropriate R9-R12; serial mode populate R13/R14. It doesn't explicitly say R3/R4 removed in serial mode. But R3/R4 are 1k series, so even if present, they connect bus to /PWM1/2 nets which may be unconnected if R9-R12 open. That's okay. If R9-R12 populated too, then bus tied to GPIO pins, bad. But assembly choice. Not anomaly.

Potential issue: R9-R12 mapping. Spec says "Short R10, R10 for Core2 and CoreS3 / Short R9, R11 for others" (typo). Netlist: R9 connects /PWM1 to pin19; R10 connects /PWM1 to pin21. Potential issue: U1 pin2 ~RE and pin3 DE tied together. Correct for half-duplex. R7 20k pull-down to GND. Q2 collector drives. When Q2 off, R7 pulls low -> receiver enabled. When Q2 on, collector high -> driver enabled. Correct.

Potential issue: Q2 emitter to +3V3, base via R2 to /TXD2, R1 from +3V3 to /TXD2. Wait R1 is between +3V3 and /TXD2, not between base and emitter. So /TXD2 is pulled up to 3.3V via 10k. R2 from /TXD2 to base. This means base is driven by /TXD2 through 5.1k, and /TXD2 has 10k pull-up. When TXD2 is high (3.3V), base is at 3.3V (no current), Q2 off. When TXD2 low (0V), base pulled low through R2, but R1 pulls /TXD2 up. The voltage at /TXD2 when driven low by UART? UART output low can sink. Base current = (3.3 - Vbe - V_TXD2)/R2? Actually /TXD2 is driven low by UART, so 0V. Base current = (3.3 - 0.7)/5.1k = 0.51mA. Q2 turns on. R1 10k from 3.3 to /TXD2 adds 0.33mA load when low. Fine. When TXD2 high, Q2 off. Correct.

Potential issue: U1 pin4 DI connected directly to /TXD2. Correct.

Potential issue: U1 pin1 RO connected to /RXD2. Correct.

Potential issue: U1 pin6 A connected to /TTL, which is also R6 pull-up to +3V3. U1 pin7 B has R8 pull-up and R15 pull-down. As noted, B is biased to 1.65V. A is pulled to 3.3V. When driver disabled, A=3.3, B=1.65, receiver sees high (A>B). When driver enabled, A and B driven complementary. But B is not connected to bus, so the bus only sees A. The receiver sees A vs B. If B is fixed at 1.65, then A high >1.65 -> high, A low <1.65 -> low. So it works as a single-ended receiver with threshold 1.65. The driver drives A and B; B is loaded by 1.1k to 1.65, so when A low, B high, but B not on bus. The bus sees A. This is a hack to use RS-485 as single-ended. Is that intended? The spec says "shared half-duplex TTL serial bus, driven through a MAX3485 RS-485/RS-422 transceiver". It might be exactly this. But why R8 pull-up on B? To set threshold. If B were only pulled down to GND, threshold 0? Actually receiver differential threshold is 0V, so B at 0 would make A high if >0. But with B at 0, when A low 0, differential 0, indeterminate. So B needs mid-supply to provide threshold. Thus R8 and R15 form a mid-supply bias for B. That makes sense! So R8 pull-up and R15 pull-down on B is intentional to create a reference voltage for single-ended use. A has pull-up R6 to fail-safe high. So not anomaly. Good.

Potential issue: R6 2k pull-up on A to +3V3. When driver drives A low, it must sink current through R6 (1.65mA) plus servo input. Fine. When driver disabled, A high. Good.
